text: Each generator has one homogeneous degree, so projecting it gives itself or zero. Projection is additive and R-linear, hence preserves its R-span. This proves closure under every homogeneous component, the condition used in [Stacks’ degreewise submodule/quotient convention](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00JL). Semirings and arbitrary index types suffice; an empty generating set gives the zero submodule. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Balanced/Grading/Basic.lean#L84) passes.
The actual balancing relation span is homogeneous for total degree.

The degree-p carrier is U∩Gₚ, expressed by comap along the R-linear inclusion. Homogeneity ensures every component stays in U; uniqueness and finite support are inherited from the ambient decomposition. This realizes [Stacks’ degreewise submodule/quotient convention](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00JL). U may be an S-submodule: scalar restriction, rather than an unsupported S-grading, supplies the R-pieces. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Quotient.lean#L111) passes.
Inherited submodule membership is exactly ambient homogeneous membership.
Including a homogeneous component from the submodule gives the ambient component.

The comap is precisely the inverse image of Gₚ under U↪M, hence the degree-p part of U. Restricting scalars changes no underlying inclusion. This is the intersection description behind [Stacks’ degreewise submodule/quotient convention](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00JL) and remains meaningful over semirings, without freeness or a chosen basis. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Quotient.lean#L111) passes.
Inherited submodule membership is exactly ambient homogeneous membership.

For x already in U, belonging to its inherited degree-p piece means exactly that its ambient value belongs to Gₚ. No second membership assumption or equality of S- and R-module structures is needed. The statement is the elementwise form of [Stacks’ degreewise submodule/quotient convention](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00JL); the published component-projection equation checks the same inclusion. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Quotient.lean#L115) passes.
Including a homogeneous component from the submodule gives the ambient component.

The inclusion preserves each degree and is injective, so uniqueness of the internal direct-sum decomposition identifies the two degree-p components. This is the degreewise submodule compatibility in [Stacks’ degreewise submodule/quotient convention](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00JL). The equation compares ambient values, not unequal subtype carriers; it needs no finite-dimensionality or canonical basis. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Quotient.lean#L153) passes.
Kernel projection agrees with the ambient source projection.

A homogeneous map sends degree p to p+r. Right cancellation makes this degree shift injective, so f(x)=0 forces the images of all homogeneous components to vanish separately. Its kernel therefore inherits the source grading, as in [Stacks’ degreewise submodule/quotient convention](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00JL). The kernel remains an S-module with R-graded pieces; r need not be zero. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Quotient.lean#L146) passes.
A kernel element has precisely its ambient source degree.
Kernel projection agrees with the ambient source projection.

A kernel element already includes the equation f(z)=0. The remaining degree-p condition is exactly membership of its ambient value in Gₚ, with no degree-r shift on the source. This agrees with [Stacks’ degreewise submodule/quotient convention](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00JL) and the published equation identifying kernel projections with ambient projections. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Quotient.lean#L153) passes.
Kernel projection agrees with the ambient source projection.

Degree p is the image of Gₚ under M→M/U, so it represents Gₚ/(Gₚ∩U), the quotient convention of [Stacks’ degreewise submodule/quotient convention](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00JL). Homogeneity of U makes these images independent; surjectivity makes them span. Restricting the S-linear quotient map to R preserves its carrier. The construction needs neither flatness nor a complement of U. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Quotient.lean#L191) passes.
A quotient class has degree p exactly when it has a degree-p representative.
Taking a homogeneous component commutes with the canonical quotient map.
The actual A∞ cohomology grading consists of classes of homogeneous cycles.

Submodule.map gives the image of Gₚ under the actual quotient map, not an arbitrary selected representative. This is the degreewise quotient in [Stacks’ degreewise submodule/quotient convention](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00JL). The R-scalar restriction retains the S-module quotient carrier, and the source-present membership and component equations verify that interpretation. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Quotient.lean#L191) passes.
A quotient class has degree p exactly when it has a degree-p representative.
Taking a homogeneous component commutes with the canonical quotient map.

Membership in the quotient degree-p image is equivalent to having some degree-p representative. It does not claim every representative is homogeneous or that a representative is unique. This is exactly [Stacks’ degreewise submodule/quotient convention](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00JL) at the element level; the published component formula ensures projection commutes with taking the quotient class. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Quotient.lean#L209) passes.
Taking a homogeneous component commutes with the canonical quotient map.

On homogeneous a,m,n, both (ma)⊗n and m⊗(an) have degree |a|+|m|+|n|. Decomposing arbitrary inputs shows all balancing relations are spanned by these homogeneous ones. Their span is therefore homogeneous, giving precisely the relation space in [Stacks’ graded tensor construction](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09LL). The opposite algebra records the right action without reversing its degree. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Balanced/Grading/Basic.lean#L104) passes.
Each balanced degree piece is the image of the ground-ring tensor degree piece.

The quotient of the ground-ring tensor by homogeneous balancing relations inherits total degree, agreeing with [Stacks’ graded tensor construction](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09LL) and [Keller §6.1](https://www.numdam.org/item/ASENS_1994_4_27_1_63_0.pdf#page=20). The source permits separately specified scalar actions: its carrier is the R-linear balanced quotient, and compatible actions recover the usual algebra-relative tensor. No flatness, finite dimension, or derived-tensor assertion is hidden. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Balanced/Grading/Basic.lean#L117) passes.
A balanced degree piece is generated by pure tensors whose two degrees sum to it.
The actual balanced pure tensor of degrees p,q has degree p+q.

The degree-p piece is the image of the ground-ring total-degree piece under the canonical balanced quotient map. This is the cokernel description in [Stacks’ graded tensor construction](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09LL). It includes all finite sums of homogeneous pure tensors of total degree p, rather than claiming every homogeneous tensor is pure. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Balanced/Grading/Basic.lean#L111) passes.
Balanced homogeneous classes admit same-degree ground-ring tensor representatives.
A balanced degree piece is generated by pure tensors whose two degrees sum to it.

A balanced class has degree p exactly when it admits a homogeneous ground-ring tensor representative of that degree. The existential witness is a tensor, not necessarily a pure tensor, and need not be unique. This matches the homogeneous quotient underlying [Stacks’ graded tensor construction](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09LL); the published degree-sum formula identifies its generating pure tensors. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Balanced/Grading/Basic.lean#L117) passes.
A balanced degree piece is generated by pure tensors whose two degrees sum to it.

Submodule.map₂ spans images of pairs in G_q and H_(p−q); the supremum over q collects their finite sums. Thus the formula says total degree is p, exactly as in [Stacks’ graded tensor construction](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09LL). It does not make an infinite-sum convergence claim or require nonnegative degrees. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Balanced/Grading/Basic.lean#L134) passes.
The homogeneous pure-tensor condition extends to every element of the source degree piece.

The canonical quotient sends m⊗n of ground-ring degree p+q to the balanced pure tensor in that same degree. This is the graded balanced-map rule of [Stacks’ graded tensor construction](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09LL). The statement allows zero factors, whose tensor lies in every degree, and claims membership rather than a unique degree of zero. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Balanced/Grading/Basic.lean#L172) passes.
The actual equivariant tensor map has the sum of the factor-map degrees.

Each degree-p piece is spanned by homogeneous pure tensors with degrees q and p−q. R-linearity therefore extends the given shift-s rule to the whole piece. This follows from the graded generating description in [Stacks’ graded tensor construction](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09LL). Target pieces need only be submodules; their own direct-sum decomposition is unnecessary. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Balanced/Grading/Basic.lean#L149) passes.
Pure-tensor degree control suffices for homogeneity of the whole linear map.

The pure-tensor hypothesis extends by linearity to every source degree piece, and IsHomogeneous packages exactly that shifted membership condition. This is the graded universal-property reasoning of [Stacks’ graded tensor construction](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09LL). No decomposition of the target family is assumed, and s may be any integer. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Balanced/Grading/Basic.lean#L172) passes.
The actual equivariant tensor map has the sum of the factor-map degrees.

On m⊗n the defined map is f(m)⊗g(n), with degree (p+r)+(q+s)=(p+q)+(r+s). Equivariance with both A-actions makes it descend through balancing. This verifies the degree bookkeeping of [Stacks’ graded tensor construction](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09LL) for this explicitly unsigned map. It does not assert the Koszul-signed tensor rule for arbitrary DG morphisms. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Balanced/Basic.lean#L210) passes.
The tensor map really evaluates to f(m)⊗g(n), with no added Koszul sign.

The new [PolishSpace hypothesis](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Polish.lean#L62) concerns the topology, so the chosen extended pseudometric need not be complete. Its distance-power cost is still continuous for every real exponent by [ENNReal.continuous_rpow_const](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Continuity.lean#L468); [Villani Theorem4.1 and Remark4.4](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=49) therefore still gives attainment, possibly at ∞. Rechecked Layer1 controls pass: [2×2 interval and all cost cases](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Finite/TwoByTwo.lean#L133), [terminating uncrossing](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Finite/Uncrossing/Termination.lean#L201), [power costs](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Finite/PowerCost.lean#L40) and [closed barriers](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Cost/Constraint.lean#L115). This generalization asserts existence of a minimizing joint measure, with no finite-moment or metric claim for unrestricted p.

Published distance-cost instance of optimal-plan existence.

[Cohen, Definition 1.4.8](https://ebooks.karbust.me/Mathematics/Henri%20Cohen%20-%20A%20Course%20in%20Computational%20Algebraic%20Number%20Theory%20%281993%29%20%5B978-3-662-02945-9%5D.pdf#page=48) agrees with the zero, sign and 2-adic conventions. Beyond the prior formula review, the published [multiplicativity theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/NumberTheory/LegendreSymbol/KroneckerSymbol.lean#L148) correctly excludes zero denominator factors: numerator −1 and factors 0,3 otherwise give 1=−1. The [gcd criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/NumberTheory/LegendreSymbol/KroneckerSymbol.lean#L191) includes zero denominators, and the [character evaluation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/NumberTheory/LegendreSymbol/KroneckerSymbol.lean#L398) retains D≠0 and D≡0,1 mod4. These source-present controls satisfy the symbol-specific roadmap requirements.
Actual nonzero-factor multiplicativity, with both guards.
Actual unrestricted-factor multiplicativity when numerator differs from −1.
Vanishing iff gcd differs from1, including zero arguments.
Published character evaluates to the symbol under nonzero discriminant congruence hypotheses.

The nonsquare hypothesis makes R(i)/R proper, exactly the condition in [Artin–Schreier’s characterization, Theorem21](https://homepages.math.uic.edu/~noquez/pdfs/thesis.pdf#page=16). The proof identifies the given quadratic field with R(i); square-root coordinates establish closure of squares under addition and the odd-degree root property. The published [AdjoinRoot specialization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/FieldTheory/RealClosure/QuadraticExtension.lean#L158) passes and explicitly requires irreducibility of X²+1, preventing a quotient with zero divisors. No order, Archimedean or completeness hypothesis is needed.
Actual specialization to X²+1 with explicit irreducibility and resulting quadratic field instance.

[Stacks00H8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00H8) states the domain case; [author comment4410](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00H8#comment-4410) gives the broader minimal-prime reduction used here. Torsion freeness forces each minimal prime of S to contract to zero; passing to S/P gives an integral domain extension, then prime pullback proves going down. The published [regular-sequence consumer](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/RingTheory/CohenMacaulay/RegularSequence.lean#L196) passes without assuming S is a domain. The zero algebra causes only the legitimate absence of primes.
Actual finite torsion-free algebra consumer invokes going down in the localization dimension comparison, without domain B.
Actual dimension-two regular-sequence consumer uses going down before Cohen–Macaulay specialization.

The normalization has real content: from F=eω and F(0)=1, the source forms the unit e(0), sets P=e(0)ω and G=e(0)⁻¹e, and proves G entire by entire division. Thus P(0)=G(0)=1; G⁻¹ is required only at radius c. This is the normalized consequence of [Martin, Corollary 1.28](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/32152#page=18), whose multiplicative-unit hypothesis matches `IsMulDistinguished` without requiring the whole ring norm multiplicative. [Coleman A3](https://kundudeb.github.io/1997_Coleman.pdf#page=16) supplies the entire-series setting, not this exact theorem verbatim. The [roadmap subtarget](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4adc7e3d0b68a8bb9974126e7411667cb533255f/TauCetiRoadmap/RestrictedPowerSeries/README.md#L766) passes through the published monic comparison, uniqueness, coprimality and smaller-radius theorems. The preceding resultant checks and subsequent series-classification checks concern other subtargets. No local compilation.
The constant-normalized polynomial rescales the actual monic Weierstrass polynomial.
Equality of the two normalized factors.
The same preparation restricts to every smaller absolute radius.
The factors generate the unit ideal in the entire-series ring.

[Bosch, §3.1 Theorem 15](https://math.bu.edu/people/yangzhe/Bosch_FormalRigidGeometry.pdf#page=44) proves attainment by reducing to a minimal prime and a finite Tate normalization; the inspected Lean statement has exactly those classical points. `pointNorm` uses the unique extended norm on the finite residue field, so a K-rational point is not presumed. The [boundedness theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/RingTheory/Affinoid/SupSeminorm.lean#L281) prevents the real supremum from taking an unbounded-set default. Nilpotents are allowed: the kernel theorem and [nonzero square-zero example](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Examples/RingTheory/Affinoid/MinimalPolynomial.lean#L50) give supremum zero. Of the [§2.2 checks](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4adc7e3d0b68a8bb9974126e7411667cb533255f/TauCetiRoadmap/RigidAnalyticGeometry/README.md#L317), this nilpotent family passes; the annulus domain/multiplicativity, product maximum-locus density and zero-algebra power checks concern different assertions. `Nontrivial A` is necessary for the existential point. No local compilation.
Point values are bounded, so the real supremum has the intended mathematical value.
Every nilpotent in every affinoid algebra has supremum zero.
A source-present nonzero square-zero element in Tate dual numbers has supremum zero.

The [source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Analysis/BoundedVariation/Space.lean#L238) installs the full BV norm, and its finite-variation carrier makes `toReal` legitimate. The [completeness instance](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Analysis/BoundedVariation/Space.lean#L306) controls variation of differences along an L¹ limit; it therefore proves completeness in that full norm. This matches [Ambrosio–Fusco–Pallara, Proposition 3.6 and p.121](https://djvu.online/file/YKj4359XUuIAE). The [G3 wrapper controls](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4adc7e3d0b68a8bb9974126e7411667cb533255f/TauCetiRoadmap/GeometricMeasureTheory/README.md#L193) pass: a.e. extensionality, representative reconstruction, exact norm and continuous injective L¹ inclusion are source-present. Integrability excludes the undefined-integral issue in the raw variation functional. Haar measure is needed for the classical interpretation, as documented; arbitrary measures remain an intentional variational generalization. Geometric derivative/perimeter and Cantor examples test separate constructions. No local compilation.
Almost-everywhere equality on Ω is equality of BV classes.
Reconstructing from the chosen representative gives the original BV element.
The actual installed norm is L1 plus real-valued total variation.
Variation is finite before conversion with ENNReal.toReal.
Completeness holds for the BV norm, not merely for the ambient L1 norm.
The continuous linear map into actual Mathlib L1 is injective.
For Haar measure the variation agrees with the integral of the weak gradient norm.

[HPT Corollary A.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1509.02937#page=45) gives two correspondences; the [explicit inverse Drinfeld formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Rigid/Drinfeld.lean#L104) selects their first, equation (31), which is equation (3) of the roadmap. Lean’s `φ ≫ u⁻¹` means the usual `u⁻¹ ∘ φ`. Both [round trips](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Pivotal/OfBalanced.lean#L88) are equalities of the actual structures, not just an existence equivalence. The [Layer 10 controls](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4adc7e3d0b68a8bb9974126e7411667cb533255f/TauCetiRoadmap/PivotalSpherical/README.md#L609) pass, including the published canonical symmetric-family identity-twist theorem. Its instance is fixed canonically; an arbitrary pivotal structure on a symmetric category is not asserted to have trivial twist. Ribbon dual compatibility and semisimplicity belong to separate results. No local compilation.
The explicit inverse Drinfeld composite has the positive braiding and evaluation order of HPT equation (3)/(31).
Pivotal → twist → pivotal is equality of structures.
Twist → pivotal → twist is equality of structures.
Every symmetric rigid category with the canonical pivotal instance has identity twist; this is the actual published family covering the symmetric example.

The [original second-edition §6.2.2, p.241](https://lib.ysu.am/disciplines_bk/846630ed4821ff13bac74569abc50312.pdf#page=258) distinguishes total draws from failures; shifting by r gives this convention. The published [zero-success](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/NegativeHypergeometric/Basic.lean#L226), [invalid-parameter](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/NegativeHypergeometric/Basic.lean#L142) and [exact-support](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/NegativeHypergeometric/Basic.lean#L220) checks pass, including the empty and all-success populations. The support guard is essential because natural subtraction truncates. [Mass](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/NegativeHypergeometric/Basic.lean#L198), [normalization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/NegativeHypergeometric/Basic.lean#L173) and [parameter-measurability](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/NegativeHypergeometric/Basic.lean#L136) checks also pass. Roadmap §9.3 specifies these boundaries; its separate permutation/cdf bridges are not claims of this definition.
At r=0 and K≤N, the law is δ0; includes the empty population.
Outside r≤K≤N the totalized measure is zero.
Exact support: k≤N−K and either k=0 or r>0; includes the all-success population.
The real singleton mass is the classical binomial ratio on support and zero elsewhere.
Normalization holds under the exact valid hypotheses r≤K≤N, including r=0.
The full three-parameter totalized family is measurable.
